zones.name: Gnosticism
zones.subtitle: Sethian & Valentinian · 2nd–4th c. CE
zones.blurb: The classical Gnostic schools of Valentinus, Basilides and the Sethians. What the Fathers quoted — and what G.R.S. Mead recovered from the Askew Codex — is public-domain; the codices dug up in the 20th century are not.

zones.name: Manichaeism
zones.subtitle: Mani’s world religion · 3rd c. CE, Rome to China
zones.blurb: Once a rival to Christianity from North Africa to China, now wholly extinct. Mani wrote his own scriptures — and almost none survive in public-domain English; the church is visible mainly through the Fathers who condemned it.

zones.name: Mandaeism
zones.subtitle: the last living Gnostics · Iraq & Iran
zones.blurb: The only Gnostic religion to survive to the present day — and, strikingly, the one with no public-domain English scripture at all. Its holy books exist in English only in modern copyrighted or German editions.

zones.name: Dualist heresies & the late-antique fringe
zones.subtitle: Cathars, Bogomils, Paulicians, Marcionites
zones.blurb: The medieval dualist churches and the great late-antique heresies. Two survive in surprising public-domain English (the Cathar Secret Supper and the Paulician Key of Truth); the rest are © or unrecovered.
